name: Stalinism
summary: Stalinism is the system of rule built in the Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin from the late 1920s to 1953. It combined socialism in one country, a planned state-owned economy, forced collectivization and rapid industrialization with a one-party state, a personality cult and mass repression justified by an intensifying class struggle. Its adherents present it as Marxism-Leninism.
scope: The Soviet system of 1927-1953 under Joseph Stalin, as the defining reference works describe it (Britannica, the Library of Congress country study, the Marxists Internet Archive glossary) and as its 1936 Constitution sets it out. Answers rest on the regime's record (sources tagged action) and on the 1936 Constitution; Stalin's own speeches and works are not cited because no defining source names them. It excludes Trotskyism, Maoism, Hoxhaism and post-1956 de-Stalinised Marxism-Leninism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Article 132 of the 1936 Constitution makes universal military service law and Article 133 makes defending the fatherland a sacred duty (s7).

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of origin and ended titles of the old order.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: In 1944 only registered marriages were recognized as legal (s10).

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The NKVD secret police stepped up surveillance and ran the purges, and forced-labour camps became an integral part of the economy (s8, s10).

abortion-legal.rationale: The state abolished abortion in the 1930s as part of strengthening the family and in 1936 made abortions and divorces more difficult to obtain (s10).

accelerate-technology.rationale: Stalin's industrialization drive was pursued as a 'revolution from above', imposing rapid change on the economy and society (s10).

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution makes the land state property, belonging to the whole people (s7).

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church and state and equal rights for all; Stalinist practice persecuted religion but did not legislate against apostasy.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: From 1936 to 1939 the Soviet Union assisted antifascists in the Spanish Civil War, and after 1945 it assisted local communist parties in coming to power (s10).

arms-reduction.rationale: Military expenditures increased dramatically during the 1930s and the standing army was expanded in 1939 (s10).

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Stalin identified political opposition with treason and used this against Trotsky, Bukharin and their supporters (s8).

bound-labor.rationale: Collectivization restricted the peasants' movements from the collective farms, in effect reintroducing a kind of serfdom (s10).

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Supreme Soviet formally approved the budget, but real control lay with the party, so adherents saw approval as a formality rather than a check.

capital-controls.rationale: Article 14(h) of the 1936 Constitution puts foreign trade on a state monopoly and Article 14(n) puts the monetary and credit system under Union direction (s7).

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees care and support through state social insurance and state-run services, so the state, not charity, is meant to provide for the poor.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Stalinist rule vested decisions in the party and state organs, not citizens chosen by lot; the 1936 constitution provides for elected soviets only.

civil-marriage.rationale: In 1944 only registered marriages were recognized as legal (s10).

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Stalinism held that the enemies of socialism within and without Russia would try to avert the final victory of the revolution, and the purges followed from that view (s8).

clerical-rule.rationale: Churches were closed from 1929 and clergy persecuted, particularly in the late 1930s (s10).

collective-bargaining.rationale: Trade unions were converted into extensions of the industrial ministries and workers came under strict labor codes (s10).

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivization compounded the peasants' lands and animals into collective farms and abolished private farms (s10), and Article 7 of the 1936 Constitution makes the collective farm a basic form of socialist property (s7).

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The Marxists Internet Archive glossary names the idea of revolution in stages, a national-democratic revolution before the socialist one, as a main tenet of Stalinist politics (s11).

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave equal rights regardless of religion or nationality, and one-party rule left no room for religious electorates.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Authority was centralized in Moscow and the self-governing powers of the republics curtailed (s10).

conscription.rationale: Article 132 of the 1936 Constitution makes universal military service law (s7).

cooperative-communities.rationale: The First Five-Year Plan organized the peasantry into collective units that the authorities could easily control, not self-governing communities replacing the state (s10).

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Article 124 of the 1936 Constitution separates the school from the church, leaving no place for religious accounts of origins in state schools (s7).

death-penalty.rationale: At three publicized show trials in Moscow between 1936 and 1938 dozens of Old Bolsheviks confessed and were executed (s10).

decide-locally.rationale: Centralized authority in Moscow was strengthened and the self-governing powers of the republics were curtailed (s10).

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Article 2 of the 1936 Constitution presents the achievement of the dictatorship of the proletariat as the base from which the Soviets grew (s7).

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Stalinist doctrine defined discrimination by class and intent under the 1936 constitution's equality of rights, not by outcome statistics.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Stalinism was officially atheist and grounded authority in the working class as led by the party; the 1936 Constitution says power belongs to the working people.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Article 3 of the 1936 Constitution vests all power in the Soviets of Working People's Deputies, and Article 30 makes the Supreme Soviet the highest organ of state authority (s7).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The purges of 1936-38 brought show trials at which Old Bolsheviks confessed to improbable crimes and were executed, and unpublicized purges after which millions had been executed, imprisoned or exiled (s10).

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Article 123 of the 1936 Constitution punishes any establishment of direct or indirect privileges on account of race or nationality (s7).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1936 Constitution lists citizens' rights (Chapter X), but the Supreme Soviet itself may amend it (s7).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article 123 of the 1936 Constitution makes equal rights irrespective of nationality or race an indefeasible law (s7), while whole nationalities were deported against their constitutional rights (s10).

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 17 nominally allowed secession, but the regime crushed nationalist movements and deported peoples; practice favoured keeping territory.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land was nationalised and no foreigner could own it under the Soviet system.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Articles 120 and 121 of the 1936 Constitution provide free medical service for the working people and education, including higher education, free of charge (s7).

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Article 11 of the 1936 Constitution subjects the whole economy to a single state national economic plan (s7).

free-public-college.rationale: Article 121 of the 1936 Constitution makes education, including higher education, free of charge (s7), but Stalin's government introduced tuition fees for higher education in 1940, so doctrine and practice diverge.

free-trade.rationale: Article 14(h) of the 1936 Constitution puts foreign trade on the basis of a state monopoly (s7).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The 1936 constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of nationality or race, and private enterprise was abolished, so private discrimination has no place.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights of women but set no representation quotas.

gradual-change.rationale: Stalin's 'revolution from above' imposed rapid industrialization and forced collectivization on a population that resisted (s10).

homestead-ownership.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution makes the land state property (s7).

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The 1936 Constitution states the socialist principle 'from each according to his ability, to each according to his work' and bars income from ownership of means of production.

independent-unions.rationale: Under the First Five-Year Plan the trade unions were converted into mechanisms for raising productivity and served as extensions of the industrial ministries (s10).

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Article 120 of the 1936 Constitution ensures maintenance in old age through social insurance at state expense (s7).

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Stalinism held that class struggle is the basic cleavage and that the 1936 Constitution had abolished exploitation; separate or overlapping oppressions were treated as secondary.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1936 constitution guarantees the right to work and the planned economy was meant to provide employment for all.

leader-cult.rationale: Stalin was recognized as the sole infallible interpreter of party ideology and the reverence accorded him gradually eclipsed that given to Lenin (s8, s10).

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Article 12 of the 1936 Constitution makes work a duty of every able-bodied citizen, on the principle 'he who does not work, neither shall he eat' (s7).

limit-population.rationale: The state paid women with large families from 1936 and in 1942 taxed single and childless persons, aiming to raise births (s10).

local-essentials-public.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution makes municipal enterprises and communications state property (s7).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Article 11 of the 1936 Constitution has the economy determined and directed by the state national economic plan (s7), and the economy was centralized under Gosplan (s10).

means-match-ends.rationale: Socialism was pursued by terror, forced collectivization against resistance and forced-labour camps made an integral part of the economy (s8).

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: Article 20 of the 1936 Constitution says an all-Union law prevails over a conflicting Union Republic law, and the republics' self-governing powers were curtailed (s7, s10).

military-guardian-role.rationale: Stalin jailed or executed about 30,000 Red Army officers and restored the dual command authority of political commissars, keeping the army under party control (s10).

military-superiority.rationale: The Five-Year Plans built the productive base to modernize the Red Army, and the Soviet Union emerged from the war as one of the world's two great military powers (s10).

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The 1936 Constitution organizes nationalities into Union Republics, with the republics keeping their own constitutions and territory unaltered without consent (s7).

mixed-constitution.rationale: Article 3 of the 1936 Constitution vests all power in the working people through the Soviets (s7).

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Article 4 of the 1936 Constitution abrogates private ownership of the means of production, and Article 6 makes banks, communications and municipal enterprises state property (s7).

moral-incentives.rationale: Higher pay and privileges accrued to productive workers and labour brigades, and Stalin denounced 'levelers' and set up systems of reward (s10, s8).

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion suffered from state repression from 1929, with churches closed, a five-year plan against religion declared and clergy persecuted in the late 1930s (s10).

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: Article 4 of the 1936 Constitution abrogates private ownership of the means of production, so municipal enterprises (Article 6) operate with no private firms beside them (s7).

municipal-property.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution makes municipal enterprises state property belonging to the whole people (s7).

nation-first.rationale: The Soviet Union refused Marshall Plan aid and forbade the countries it dominated from taking part (s10).

national-church-status.rationale: Article 124 of the 1936 Constitution separates the church from the state (s7).

national-mission.rationale: After the war the Soviet Union actively assisted local communist parties in coming to power in the Eastern European countries it occupied (s10).

national-resource-control.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution makes the land and its natural deposits state property (s7).

national-self-determination.rationale: The 1936 Constitution reserves the right to secede to Union Republics (s7), but non-Russian elites were purged, republics lost self-governing powers and nationalities were deported (s10).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Article 4 of the 1936 Constitution declares the socialist system of economy the economic foundation of the USSR (s7).

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The 1936 constitution separated church from state, and the regime suppressed religious organisation of any kind.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The state made divorces more difficult to obtain from 1936 and in 1944 made divorce subject to the court's discretion (s10).

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Article 124 of the 1936 Constitution separates the school from the church (s7).

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The 1936 Constitution fills the Soviets by elections of deputies (s7).

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 126 of the 1936 Constitution names the Communist Party the leading core of all public and state organizations (s7), and the party retained all political power (s10).

parliament-supreme.rationale: Supreme Soviet was nominally the supreme body under the 1936 constitution but the party actually ruled; ambiguous.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The 1936 Constitution framed Soviet democracy through soviets and the party, while Stalinism rejected independent initiative from below as a threat; participation was directed from the centre.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stalin restored the dual command authority of political commissars in Red Army units and kept the army under party control (s10).

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Stalin's doctrine of the monolithic party condemned the 'rotten liberalism' of those who tolerated discussion of or dissent from party policies (s8).

party-own-road.rationale: The Comintern ordered the Communist Party of Germany to aid the Nazi Party in its bid for power (s10).

person-over-state.rationale: The regime practised terror, abolished private farms and businesses, and regimented society, treating individuals as means to its goals (s8, s10).

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Article 10 of the 1936 Constitution protects personal ownership of income, savings, homes and articles of personal use while the means of production are socialist property.

population-transfer.rationale: Whole nationalities were deported during World War II and many were punished as traitors (s10).

positive-liberty.rationale: Article 125 of the 1936 Constitution ensures civil rights by placing printing presses, paper, public buildings and communications at the disposal of the working people (s7).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The regime glorified Russian history and traditions while executing or deporting the intellectual and cultural elites of other nations such as Ukraine (s10).

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed press and assembly by placing printing presses and halls at the disposal of workers, on the premise that the bourgeoisie had controlled them.

production-for-use.rationale: Article 11 of the 1936 Constitution directs the economy by plan to increase public wealth and improve the material conditions of the working people (s7).

profit-exploitation.rationale: Article 4 of the 1936 Constitution presents the abrogation of private ownership of the means of production as the abolition of the exploitation of man by man (s7).

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: From 1936 the government paid women with large families, and in 1942 it taxed single and childless married persons (s10).

property-franchise.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave universal and equal suffrage to all citizens and abolished the property and class disqualifications that the earlier constitution had imposed.

property-fundamental.rationale: The regime abolished private farms and businesses and liquidated the kulaks (s10).

public-money-creation.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution makes banks state property and Article 14(n) puts the monetary and credit system under Union direction (s7).

public-ownership.rationale: Articles 4 to 6 of the 1936 Constitution make the land, mines, factories, banks and transport state property belonging to the whole people (s7).

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1936 Constitution proclaimed equal rights for citizens regardless of nationality or race and made any racial privilege a punishable offence.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Stalinism held that class, not race, defined political interests, and the 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of race.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Article 123 of the 1936 Constitution makes equal rights irrespective of nationality or race an indefeasible law and punishes any restriction of rights on account of race (s7).

recall-officials.rationale: Article 142 of the 1936 Constitution makes a deputy liable to be recalled at any time by a majority of the electors (s7).

region-keeps-system.rationale: The republics were formally autonomous but all shared one socialist legal and economic system under Party direction.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: Article 6 of the 1936 Constitution makes the land and its natural deposits state property belonging to the whole people (s7).

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church and state and guarantees equal rights, though in practice religion was repressed.

religious-nation.rationale: The Soviet state was officially atheist and the 1936 constitution separates church and state, so the nation is not defined by religion.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Article 123 of the 1936 Constitution makes equal rights irrespective of nationality or race an indefeasible law (s7).

restore-past-order.rationale: The regime remade the economy and society by collectivization and industrialization, but its social policy of the 1930s returned to conservative norms and glorified Russia's past (s10).

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rapid industrialization and collectivization were carried out alongside the suppression of dissent (s10).

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 17 of the 1936 Constitution reserves to every Union Republic the right freely to secede (s7), but the regime curtailed the republics' self-government and deported whole nationalities against their constitutional rights (s10).

second-chamber.rationale: The 1936 Constitution created a Supreme Soviet with two chambers, the Soviet of the Union and the Soviet of Nationalities.

self-ownership.rationale: Collectivization restricted the peasants' movements, in effect reintroducing a kind of serfdom, and forced-labour camps were made an integral part of the economy (s8, s10).

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 124 of the 1936 Constitution separates church from state and school from church (s7), while the state repressed religion, closing churches from 1929 (s10).

separated-powers.rationale: Power was concentrated in Stalin and the party retained all political power despite the 1936 Constitution (s8, s10).

single-official-language.rationale: Teaching the Russian language in all schools became mandatory, as part of drawing the nationalities toward Russian culture and language (s10).

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Stalin's 'revolution from above' closed churches, abolished private farms and liquidated the kulaks rather than working through established institutions (s10).

social-market-economy.rationale: Article 11 of the 1936 Constitution has the state plan direct the economy, and Article 4 abrogates private ownership of the means of production (s7).

socialism-one-country.rationale: Stalin's doctrine held that a socialist society can be built in the USSR alone, and the Marxists Internet Archive glossary names it the core of Stalinism (s11).

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Article 4 of the 1936 Constitution declares the socialist system established, with private ownership of the means of production abrogated and exploitation of man by man abolished (s7).

spiritual-nature.rationale: The regime was officially atheist and materialist and persecuted religion, though the 1936 Constitution separated church and state.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The First Five-Year Plan put the greatest share of investment into heavy industry, and the economy was centralized under Gosplan's output quotas (s10).

state-harmful.rationale: State power, far from withering away after the revolution, grew in strength under Stalin (s10).

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin held that the state must become stronger rather than wither away because the enemies of socialism would try to avert its victory (s8), and state power grew (s10).

strong-leader.rationale: From 1929 power was concentrated in Stalin personally, with a cult of personality and a monolithic party (s8); party congresses met less and less often (s10).

suppress-opposition.rationale: Stalin identified political opposition with treason, and the Old Bolsheviks were exterminated or sent to forced-labour camps (s8, s10).

surveillance-ok.rationale: The NKVD stepped up surveillance through agents and informers and claimed to uncover anti-Soviet conspiracies among long-term party members (s10).

territorial-expansion.rationale: In 1939-40 Soviet forces seized eastern Poland, entered the Baltic states, took Bessarabia and northern Bukovina and invaded Finland (s10).

total-state.rationale: Under Stalin collective enterprises replaced individual effort across the board, and the economy, the arts and science were brought under party and state control (s10).

traditional-family.rationale: To provide social stability the state aimed to strengthen the family, restricting divorce and abolishing abortion, and from 1936 paid women with large families (s10).

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: After the war the Soviet Union kept troops in the Eastern European countries it dominated, withdrawing from northern Iran in 1946 only under Western diplomatic pressure (s10).

unions-run-economy.rationale: Article 11 of the 1936 Constitution places the economy under the state plan (s7), and the trade unions were extensions of the industrial ministries (s10).

universal-healthcare.rationale: Article 120 of the 1936 Constitution guarantees maintenance in sickness through state social insurance and free medical service for the working people.

vanguard-party.rationale: The doctrine of the monolithic party was central to Stalinism and the party was subjugated to its leader (s8, s10).

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: Article 135 of the 1936 Constitution gives the vote to citizens who have reached the age of eighteen (s7).

widespread-small-property.rationale: The regime abolished private farms and businesses and compounded peasants' lands and animals into collective farms (s10).

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The 1936 constitution gave women equal rights, and Soviet law allowed divorce on request; the later 1944 restrictions complicate this.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guarantees women equal rights with men in all spheres of economic and public life, and Soviet law gave equal inheritance.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1936 Constitution gave women equal rights with men in political life, including voting and office.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Article 12 of the 1936 Constitution makes work a duty on the principle 'he who does not work, neither shall he eat' (s7).

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Article 1 of the 1936 Constitution defines the USSR as a socialist state of workers and peasants (s7).

worker-ownership.rationale: The 1936 Constitution recognizes state property and also the cooperative and collective-farm property of the members (Articles 5 and 7), but vests the main industries in the state (Article 6) (s7).

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: The glossary says Stalinism assigns the national bourgeoisie a revolutionary role and draws parties into popular fronts with progressive bourgeois elements (s11).

notes: Later pass under rules 7 (2026-11-14). The Wikipedia summary no longer supports any answer: its answers were re-sourced on the record (Library of Congress country study, Britannica) or the 1936 Constitution, or nulled (71 of them plus others whose only support was words not tied to the ideology). Stalin's own works (1939 Report, Economic Problems of the USSR, Dizzy with Success, Foundations of Leninism, Dialectical and Historical Materialism) were downloaded and read but fail the source tie check, since no defining source in the library names them by title twice, so no current answer cites them; a defining source naming them would let them back in. Themes searched: economy, government, religion, family, nationalities, war and foreign policy, security, rights. Encyclopedia.com refused scripted access and Ernest Mandel's 1952 essay would not download; both named here for the maintainer. The earlier missing statement (state strengthens under encirclement) is now covered by the statement state-strengthens-encirclement.

keyFigures.role: Soviet leader who defined the doctrine and system
keyFigures.quote: The political tenets of Stalinism revolve around the theory of socialism in one country–developed by Stalin to counter the Bolshevik theory that the survival of the Russian Revolution depended on proletarian revolutions in Europe.
